The renowned sword Autumn Waters, once fiercely contested by heroes across the martial world, was ultimately "purchased" by power. 
It passed through the hands of various "official swordsmen"—men who claimed the title of warriors yet had long abandoned their martial roots, serving powerful ministers and relying on Autumn Waters' prestige to maintain their facade. 

Many years later, a young woman recognized it, seized it, and used it to slay its then-owner. 
As it pierced its master's throat, the sword remembered the blazing forge that birthed it. It finally sang—a cry that echoed, anticipating its next strike. 

But it shattered by the waters of Peach Grove Pass. The girl snapped it in two. The fractured blade cut her hand, and once more, it tasted blood. Only when blood mingled with tears did it burn as fiercely as the forge. 
Cast into the river, it glimpsed its reflection—an ordinary sword. 
Blades grow old. It had aged long ago. 

Beware, Swordsman. The price of power steals from you unnoticed. 
Take heed, Young Man. The pinnacle of the martial world is reached by one's own hand.
